summary.text: A 67-year-old man with unresectable melanoma of the neck and lymph node metastasis, on nivolumab and ipilimumab, presented one week after the second cycle with shortness of breath, generalised muscle aches, weakness and difficulty walking. He was tachypneic and hypoxic on admission, with proximal muscle weakness, type 1 respiratory failure and an MGC score of 9.

Admission laboratory results showed elevated CK and severely elevated transaminases, with troponin I 310 ng/L; anti-AChR antibodies, liver autoantibodies and the hepatitis screen were negative. Cardiac MRI showed changes consistent with myopericarditis and MRI of spine and brain excluded metastatic disease; muscle biopsy and electrodiagnostic tests were not considered during the admission.

He received IV methylprednisolone 2 mg/kg/day, corrected to 1000 mg/day by day 6, with mycophenolate mofetil added for slow improvement. He improved, came off oxygen by day 12 and was discharged by day 15; ICIs were permanently discontinued for grade 4 myositis and myocarditis, and MMF was stopped for liver toxicity. He remained progression free one year after discharge.

summary.text: An 84-year-old man with metastatic melanoma and a remote history of prostate cancer presented two weeks after the first cycle of adjuvant pembrolizumab with severe fatigue, weakness, shortness of breath and double vision. On examination he had proximal myopathy, left eye ptosis, ophthalmoplegia and diplopia, FVC 38% and MGC score 19, with high CK and troponin (CK 5346 U/L, troponin T 4184 ng/L, troponin I 11066 ng/L).

Initial oral prednisolone was followed by IV methylprednisolone 1000 mg/day on day 2, IVIG after deterioration, and later MMF, tocilizumab, tacrolimus and pyridostigmine. Anti-AChR antibodies were negative; MRIs of quadriceps and myocardium were abandoned and plasma exchange was considered but abandoned.

He needed HDU care, non-invasive ventilation and intubation by day 12; after improvement on day 13 he was extubated but developed new atrial fibrillation and agitation, and died on day 15 of admission. Myositis, myocarditis and MG were judged grade 5 per CTCAE.

summary.text: A 68-year-old man with widely metastasised oesophageal adenocarcinoma and synchronous lung cancer developed progressive fatigue, ptosis and slurring of speech four weeks after the fourth cycle of pembrolizumab, a week after grade 1 immunotherapy-related hepatitis was diagnosed. Neuromuscular symptoms worsened with severe neck weakness and bulbar symptoms; he declined assessment and was admitted 11 days after symptom onset.

On admission he had a three-litre oxygen requirement, severe neck weakness, proximal myopathy, quadriparesis, bilateral ptosis, diplopia and slurred speech, with MGC score 14, CK 685 U/L, troponin T 707 ng/L and troponin I 244 ng/L, normal ECG and ECHO and stable cerebral metastasis on MRI. He had type 2 respiratory failure and suspected aspiration; cardiac MRI, quadriceps MRI and autoantibody screening were not completed.

IV methylprednisolone gave a very poor clinical response; MG-directed therapies were not started at the beginning, IVIG followed roughly 48 hours after admission, and tacrolimus was commenced with non-invasive ventilation and nasogastric feeding. Palliation was agreed and he died seven days after admission; irAEs were judged grade 5.

summary.text: A 60-year-old man with a history of obesity, CKD stage 1, atrial fibrillation and clear cell renal cell carcinoma metastatic to the lungs after nephrectomy presented to the emergency department with profound fatigue and shortness of breath two weeks after cycle 2 of nivolumab and ipilimumab, also reporting swallowing difficulty. Examination was unremarkable with MGC score 5 and FVC 56%.

Admitting labs showed CK 6,376 U/L, troponin T 1,694 ng/L and moderately raised transaminases, with negative anti-AChR and anti-MuSK antibodies. He received IV methylprednisolone 1000 mg/day, IVIG, pyridostigmine and MMF with cardiology input; MRI showed myocardial and quadriceps changes in keeping with myocardial inflammation and myositis.

He improved markedly by day 3 of immunosuppression, pyridostigmine was stopped as myasthenia symptoms resolved, and he was discharged by day 22 on oral prednisolone and MMF; ICIs were stopped indefinitely for grade 4 myocarditis and myositis. He remained progression free on CT two months post discharge.

article_limitations: Case series of four patients; cohort-level statements in the abstract, methods and Discussion (mean age, drug and cancer-type counts, cycle timing, "all patients received ICI therapy within four weeks of symptom onset", anti-AChR results in 3 of 4) are not copied to individuals unless a sentence names the case or all four patients explicitly.
The abstract gives a mean age of 68.9 years while the Discussion gives 69.8 years; this is a cohort-level inconsistency not attributed to any patient.

Case 1 narrative (citing Table 1) and Table 1 differ for creatine kinase (10866 vs 10389 U/L) and troponin T (498 vs 393 ng/L): paired source_conflict, review_only values; the qualitative "CK was elevated" stays scorable. Case 4 NT-proBNP unit differs (narrative ug/L vs Table 4 pg/L): both unit readings review_only, the agreed value 1369 kept as a value-only item. The Case 4 Table 4 troponin T cell printed "I694ng/L" is treated as a print ambiguity (review_only), with the narrative 1,694 ng/L kept.

Case 4 troponin I 14 ng/L appears in Table 4 (captioned admitting laboratory results) and in the narrative as resulting 4 days into the admission; recorded as one result with time null and an ambiguity.
Laboratory tables print units as given (e.g. creatinine, CRP and cortisol in mmol/L); no units were converted or corrected and no flags were derived from printed reference ranges.
Where the narrative repeats a table value for the same test and time (with or without citing the table), the two are one item citing both, per OBS-TABLE-ROWS and ONE-STATEMENT.
The Discussion statement that all four patients received inappropriately lower initial steroid doses is an authorial judgement and is kept as an ambiguity only.

Cases are not individually identified outside the case headings; unlabelled Discussion sentences (e.g. a hepatitis diagnosis, delayed MG-directed therapy) were assigned only where the sentence names the patient or case or the case text itself states the fact.
Figure captions are author statements; pixel review is in visual.json. Figure assets match their captions and the case text that calls them out.
